thread:
monitoring-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: unusual auth activity from token-proxy-2 (svc token-proxy). 401/403 spike ~1.2k req/min from 3 IPs starting 11:02 UTC. Possible token replay or leaked bearer tokens. Paging @alice_oncall @ben_sre.

alice_oncall: On it. Thanks for the ping. Paging security and SRE for triage. @chris_sec @ben_sre can you confirm if this matches the token-anomaly feed?

ben_sre: pulling logs now. quick grep shows repeated Authorization headers with similar prefix. pattern looks like repeated short-lived tokens, same header fingerprint. no 5xx increase.

ben_sre: example (redacted): `Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci...REDACTED...`

chris_sec: Marking P1. Start immediate containment: rotate service-account keys for token-proxy, blacklist suspicious tokens, and add temporary WAF blocks for the 3 IPs. @dana_legal FYI.

dana_legal: noted. Please flag if any customer PII appears in logs; we may need retention/notification steps.

alice_oncall: Ben — do logs include user identifiers or emails in headers/body? if so we need an urgent scrub.

ben_sre: sampling shows X-User-ID and occasional X-User-Email in ~12% of requests. launching scrub job now. command:```/run scrub-logs --service token-proxy --pattern "Authorization|X-User-Email|X-User-ID"```

devops-bot: Job queued: scrub-logs started (job id: scrub-17688001). Output will land in s3://redwood-security/scrub-jobs/17688001/

chris_sec: In parallel: rotate TokenProxyServiceAccount keys. Steps: 1) create new key 2) deploy, 3) delete old key. Also apply WAF rule to block `203.0.113.45`, `198.51.100.22`, `192.0.2.101` until further notice.

alice_oncall: Running rotation and WAF update now. aws command: `aws iam create-access-key --user TokenProxyServiceAccount` -> created, stored in vault. Deleted old key. WAF update returned success.

emily_cs: Any customer-facing impact? Sessions may be invalidated. Preparing standby template for customers if we need to notify.

ben_sre: After WAF + rotation traffic dropped ~80%. We still have ~60 invalidated sessions (system accounts mostly), no user-facing 5xx observed. Scrub job found 4 log entries with email addresses — started cleansing and will confirm removal.

chris_sec: Good containment. Next steps: revoke refresh tokens issued under that service account in the last 24h, add tokens to blacklist, rotate any signing keys if used, and create SEC ticket for postmortem (SEC-176880). Also schedule immediate IAM audit for sibling accounts.

dana_legal: Place retention hold on scrub output and any related S3 objects. If PII confirmed, we need timeline for notification (GDPR window noted). I'll coordinate required legal notices.

alice_oncall: Handoff: I'm off-call in 15. Ben will own stabilization & bridge, Chris will own sec follow-up/postmortem. I'm creating an incident bridge and updating status page now.

ben_sre: Acknowledged. Creating Zoom bridge, updating status page draft, and coordinating with emily_cs on comms.

emily_cs: Pls add me to the bridge. Draft template: short summary, scope (token-proxy only), mitigation (WAF + key rotation), impact (some system sessions invalidated), next steps (postmortem + audit), contact link.

monitoring-bot: ALERT RESOLVED: anomaly recovered to baseline after mitigations. Monitoring will continue for 24h.

chris_sec: Before comms, confirm scrub removed emails. Do a full check of all token-issuing services and rotate sibling keys as precaution. Assigning postmortem owner: chris_sec.

alice_oncall: Thanks team. Action items: (1) confirm scrub completion and attach verification (ben), (2) revoke tokens and rotate signing keys (chris), (3) run IAM key inventory by EOD (ben+chris), (4) prepare comms if PII confirmed (emily+dana). I'll update incident channel when off-call. :white_check_mark:
